chapter: Second European tour and the crash
title: Going home so his child would be born American
summary: With his wife pregnant and citizenship in doubt, he decides to go home at Christmas 1931.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, so, okay, we're in Copenhagen in the early '30's and you just continued through the thirties, touring and playing just about everywhere.
And did -- before we get to 1939, where -
Oh, I didn't stay there that long.
You didn't stay that long? How long did you stay?
I had a baby -- I don't mean I didn't have the baby, my wife had the baby.
So what had happened, around '32, the Christmas of '31, we started home because I didn't want my child to be born in Europe. See, because there was some doubts as to his citizenship, you know?

We was in France at the time, and there was this thing there that unless you declared the child, declared it before it was 18 or something, it would be a citizen of that country. And I didn't want no bother like that, so there wasn't nothing else for me to do. Mother was getting older, so I thought, 'Well, I'd better go home.' And another thing,
